title: More than all (Luke 20:41–21:4)
hookLine: beware showy religion; the widow gave out of her poverty

lines: THE RICH GIVE, AND PEOPLE NOTICE.
cards: A hospital lobby, and a donation wall: big brass plaques for the biggest gifts, a long list of names in tiny print at the bottom.
In the temple courts, Jesus looks up and sees the rich putting their gifts into the treasury. Large gifts. He's just warned the crowd about religion that wants to be seen.
Then a poor widow walks up and drops in two mites, tiny coins. On a plaque, her name wouldn't make the list. Jesus says something that rearranges the whole wall.

teach.h: BEWARE RELIGION THAT WANTS AN AUDIENCE.
teach.b: First the warning, in the King James words: "Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts."
He's not attacking scribes as a group; yesterday some of them told him he'd spoken well.
He's describing faith that wants an audience, and adds a harder line: they "devour widows' houses, and for a shew make long prayers." Then, straight after, a widow.
Her two coins were lepta, from a Greek word meaning small, or thin.

Jesus says: "Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had."

The gift is measured by what's left over, and she has nothing left. Readers take this two ways, and both are in the text. The familiar reading hears praise: total trust, giving from what you'd rather keep.

teach.h: ALL THE LIVING THAT SHE HAD.
teach.b: Some scholars notice where Luke put it, right after the warning about leaders who swallow up widows' houses, and hear a lament too: a system that takes a poor woman's last coins.
Either way, Jesus saw her, and Luke makes sure we do too.

how: The phrase the widow's mite comes from the King James wording of this story, and churches read it when inviting people to give, to charity or to the church, quietly and in proportion to what they have.

games.q: you're with Jesus in the temple court, watching the gifts go in. the rich give large sums; a widow drops in two tiny coins. who gave the most?
games.why: "this poor widow hath cast in more than they all": she gave all the living that she had.

practice: Think of one gift no one would ever thank you for: money given quietly, an hour of help unannounced, a kind word about someone where they'll never hear it.
Notice any wish to be seen giving it, without guilt, and picture giving it with no plaque and no audience. If you pray, offer it to God.

orig.note: Greek: small, thin. also the name of a tiny coin, the mite of the King James Bible; the widow gave two.

carryVoice: Your line: out of her poverty. A week from Zacchaeus's open door to two small coins. Day five hundred seventy-four, and another week on the path.
